message: No detected untrusted source handling: The brain_policy function fetches data from a remote URL via requests.get with no checksum verification, authentication, or integrity checks on the response.
No detected label flipping detection: No code compares label distributions, validates label values against an expected set, or uses any label-noise detection tool such as Cleanlab.

No detected data poisoning defenses: The preparation code only drops null rows and applies type/range clamping in type_conversion; there is no outlier detection, statistical anomaly check, or filtering of suspicious training samples.

No detected model integrity verification: The code loads models (e.g., via pickle or other means implied by BaseModel and the Simulator class) but there is no hash check, signature verification, or pinned revision visible anywhere in the provided code slices.
No detected label distribution validation: No code checks label distribution, class balance, or anomalous training samples before or during training.
No detected backdoor or trigger detection: There is no neural-cleanse, activation analysis, gradient anomaly detection, or any other backdoor/trigger defense in the code.
No detected differential privacy: No differential privacy libraries (Opacus, TensorFlow Privacy, DP-SGD) or mechanisms are imported or used anywhere in the code.
No detected adversarial robustness testing: No adversarial robustness testing libraries or techniques (Foolbox, ART, FGSM, PGD, etc.) are referenced or used anywhere in the code.

No detected metric tampering protection: There is no evidence of held-out test set isolation, signed/hashed evaluation data, or multiple independent metric checks to protect against metric manipulation.
No detected output bounds checks: No code in the visible inference path checks model output values for NaN, out-of-range probabilities, or any other sanity bounds before returning predictions.
No detected prompt injection defenses: This is not an LLM pipeline; the model performs numerical/tabular simulation predictions, so prompt injection defenses are not applicable and none are present.
